transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky says he's willing to hold elections if President
Trump can get Russia to suspend its attacks for 60 days.
Terry Schultz reports Zelensky also weighed in on Trump's deal to import Russian diesel
fuel.
Messing the annual Warsaw Security Forum conference, President Zelensky said while holding elections
during a war would require changing Ukrainian law, it would be possible if Russian attacks
ceased so that people could safely take part in the process.
He's heard here through an interpreter.
And it's also impossible now because of our military, more than a million people who must
vote.
But how will they vote while being on the front line?
Zelensky also suggested that instead of buying diesel from Russia, the U.S. should buy from
Ukraine.
They've been given no advance notification of the agreement with the Kremlin that Trump
announced Friday.
For NPR News, I'm Terri Schultz in Warsaw.
Three of South Carolina's candidates for U.S. Senate made their cases to voters last
night.
South Carolina public radio's Luis Alfredo Garcia reports it's their only confirmed debate
before the November midterms.
Republican Senator Darlene Graham and Democratic pediatrician Dr. Annie Andrews spent a good
chunk of their given debate time talking about each other.
Libertarian Casey Whitener mostly stuck to answering moderator questions.
But the two leading candidates did give direct, different answers on how the United States
should navigate its policy with Israel.
Graham says the country needs to stand with its "strongest ally" in the Middle East,
and she condemned Hamas.
Andrews highlighted humanitarian concerns in the region.
Israelis deserve a safe place to live, and Palestinians also deserve to live in peace.
What's happening in the region is devastating, it is a humanitarian crisis.
The winner of the race will be the first woman elected to represent South Carolina in the
Senate.
For NPR News, I'm Luis Alfredo Garcia in Columbia, South Carolina.
Stocks on Wall Street opened a mix this morning as oil prices climb.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose about 137 points in
early trading.
Crude oil prices are higher after deadly attacks over the weekend in Saudi Arabia.
Strikes by Iran-backed Houthi rebels closed the airport in the Saudi capital.
The international benchmark for crude oil is above $106 a barrel.
Retail gasoline prices showed little change overnight.
Triple A says the average price of diesel fuels down about a penny a gallon to $6.26.
President Trump's plan to buy diesel fuel from Russia is drawing pushback from a bipartisan
group of senators.
Trump announced the plan on social media last week in an effort to lower diesel prices,
but the senators complained the president did not consult with Congress.
Russia is under sanction over its invasion of Ukraine.
Scott Horsley, NPR News, Washington.
On Wall Street, the Dow was up 134 points.
This is NPR News.
Cleanup crews are clearing debris and restoring power across parts of the southeast hit by
Hurricane Esai Is. About 170,000 customers in the Florida Panhandle and southern Alabama
are still without electricity.
The storm damaged buildings and brought down trees when it struck the Gulf Coast Friday
as a category two hurricane.
At least four people have died in storm-related incidents.
Temperatures across the U.S. in September broke records this year.
NPR's Lauren Summer reports that heat is expected to continue around the world because
of a growing El Nino climate pattern.
It was the hottest September on record in the lower 48 states.
That's based on weather records that go back to 1895.
According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, it's also the third month
in a row that's been the hottest on record.
Globally, it's a similar story.
The European Union's climate service says it was the second hottest September on record.
Thanks to a super El Nino, the coming year could continue to be record-breaking.
The naturally occurring climate pattern adds extra heat to the atmosphere on top of climate
change.
El Nino years are typically the hottest years on record.
Lauren Summer, NPR News.
The Milwaukee Brewers beat the Los Angeles Dodgers 2-1 last night to take a one-game lead
in the National League Championship Series.
They'll face off tonight for Game 2.
In the American League, the Cleveland Guardians take on the Tampa Bay Rays in the series'
opener today.
On Wall Street, the Dow up 142 points, the Nasdaq down 52.
This is NPR News.
